To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) SAD phasing using an anomalous signal of only 0.6%, based on the difference between two data sets collected at different wavelengths, can be used to solve the structure of a protein, and that (2) the use of a single data set collected at the absorption edge of an element that is present in the crystal, and that has a low anomalous signal, can be used for SAD phase determination.

(1) the anomalous deltaF" signal from a Mn ion in a glucose isomerase structure is large enough to allow structure solution at 1.5 A resolution, and (2) the anomalous signal from a single Mn ion can be used for structure determination at 2.0 A resolution.

the SAD method can be used successfully to phase macromolecules with a very low anomalous signal and that the SHELXD program, which is based on direct methods, can be used for SAD structure solution of macromolecular crystals with a low anomalous signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the anomalous scattering of S and Mn atoms for phasing and refinement of glucose isomeras structures in two crystal forms.
the use of SAD methods for structure determination of proteins with a relatively low content of metal atoms, and the use of SHELXD and SHELXE for the solution and refinement of SAD structures.
the use of the anomalous signal from Mn and S in the SAD phasing procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anomalous signal is not a limiting factor for the determination of the structure of a protein by SAD phasing, provided that it can be detected by the methods used.
SAD phasing with anomalous signal as weak as 0.5% is possible, but only when the data set contains many reflections with high anomalous signal, as is the case here.
, with the current state of the art, a SAD structure determination is possible with as little as 0.5% anomalous signal, if the anomalous scatterers are well ordered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SAD phasing with the Mn sites is very robust and can be used to solve the structure of a protein from a single-wavelength anomalous signal as small as 0.5% at a wavelength of about 1 A.
, with the help of the new program suite wARP, SAD phasing can be done successfully even with a very small anomalous signal, provided the anomalous signal is not too weak.

the SAD method is a powerful tool for structure solution and that the use of multiple wavelengths and the combination of anomalous and isomorphous differences are not essential for the solution of the phase problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of multiple anomalous scatterers, the anomalous signal from the heaviest atom is the most important, even if it is not the most intense.
the SAD method is robust enough to be applied to data sets with very low anomalous signal, provided that the anomalous scattering atoms are well ordered in the crystal.
SAD phasing is not limited to data sets collected at high X-ray energies and that the SAD method is not limited to proteins with a relatively high content of anomalous scatterers.
